"''That's what I was thinking.|Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker, while the ''Twilight'' is battered by the ''Soulless One''{{'s}} laser fire|{{TCW|Destroy Malevolence|Destroy ''Malevolence''}}}} The '''''Soulless One''''' was a customized [[Feethan Ottraw Scalable Assemblies]] [[Belbullab-22 heavy starfighter|Belbullab-22]] [[starfighter]] which served as the personal [[Starship|ship]] of [[General]] [[Grievous]], [[Supreme Martial Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies|the leader]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]' [[Separatist Droid Army|Droid Army]]. However, because Grievous used the fighter to retreat, some opponents nicknamed the ship '''''Spineless One'''''. The Soulless One was reinforced with [[impervium]] alloy [[armor]], and was equipped with a [[Sensor jammer|sensor jamming system]] and two rapid fire [[laser cannon]]s. It was designed to be an upgrade to the CIS droid fighters, such as the [[Vulture-class starfighter|vulture droid]] and the [[droid tri-fighter]]s. Grievous [[Gender|himself]] preferred [[Unarmed combat|hand-to-hand combat]], although he still often flew the battle-worn fighter. After the General's [[death]] in the [[Battle of Utapau]], the ''Soulless One'' was taken by [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to escape [[Utapau]] after the [[Great Jedi Purge|execution]] of [[Order 66]]. Kenobi docked the starfighter with the ''[[Tantive III]]''. With the newborn [[Luke Skywalker]] aboard, Kenobi later used the ''Soulless One'' to travel to [[Nar Shaddaa]] and sold it for [[transport]]ation to [[Tatooine]]. ==Description== [[File:ImperviumPlating-SWZ.png|thumb|left|250px|''Soulless One'' was made with an impervium hull.]] The ''Soulless One'' was a customized [[Belbullab-22 heavy starfighter]] built by [[Feethan Ottraw Scalable Assemblies]], which had been designed as an upgrade to the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]' [[droid starfighter]]s such as the [[Vulture-class starfighter|vulture droids]] and [[droid tri-fighter]]s. The [[starfighter]] was 6.1 [[meter]]s long and 5.4 meters wide, with a [[hull]] reinforced with [[impervium]]-alloy [[armor]]. A rear-mounted thrust-vectoring fin and auxiliary thrusters incorporated into the wings aid in yaw and roll movements. Grievous' ship was a difficult client to deal with. The ''Soulless One'' was originally equipped with two single [[laser cannon]]s, but a weapons upgrade was required due to the heavy demands made on the [[cyborg]] [[general]] by his immediate superior, [[Count]] [[Dooku]], and Dooku's [[Sith Master]], [[Darth]] [[Sidious]]. Equipped with two triple rapid-fire laser cannons maintain firepower of similar destructive force to that of the Republic's [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter|V-wing starfighters]], and also contained a [[Sensor jammer|sensor-jamming system]]. [[File:SoullessOnecontrols.png|thumb|right|235px|''Soulless One'''s controls.]] Designed for a single, living [[pilot]], the [[cockpit]] possessed a [[life support]] system, although [[Grievous]] did not need it. The ''Soulless One'' had long-range scanners installed in at the front, a well-armored [[Deflector shield generator|shield generator]] directly behind the cockpit, a Class 2 [[hyperdrive]] bigger and more durable than disposable droid fighters, and a maximum [[Atmosphere|atmospheric]] speed of 1,100 [[Kilometer|kph]]. In the event of a primary hyperdrive failure, the ship was equipped with a Class 5 back up. The Belullab-22's two main ion drives allow it to keep up with a [[Rogue-class Porax-38 starfighter|Rogue-class fighter]]. Like Grievous' [[General Grievous' TSMEU-6 Wheel Bike|wheel bike]], the Belbullab-22 featured a circular, pressure-sensitive panel for controlling the ship located within a reinforced yoke, allowing most [[human]]oids to operate the ship effectively. Its owner, General Grievous, preferred [[Unarmed combat|hand-to-hand combat]] [[Gender|himself]], but still often flew the battle-worn starfighter. To keep touch with his [[Separatist Droid Army|droid armies]], a powerful, sophisticated, compact [[HoloNet]] transceiver installed in the ''Soulless One'', Grievous can access [[Galactic Republic|Republic]] and [[pirate]] networks, allowing him to oversee skirmishes and battles across the numerous warring [[sector]]s. Grievous was also able to slice into both legitimate and pirate networks, anticipating enemy activity and avoiding confrontations he couldn't win. Keeping an eye on what was happening in other sectors was an important tool for the cyborg. Grievous often directs battles from the bridge of his flagship, the ''[[Invisible Hand]]'', although a number of significant encounters were fought and directed from the cockpit of the ''Soulless One''. Therefore, the in-cockpit systems were improved to keep him in contact with his troops while operating in all corners of the [[galaxy]]. ==History== ===The Clone Wars=== The ''Soulless One'', dubbed by its owner, was in the possession of [[General]] Grievous, [[Supreme Martial Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies|commander]] of the [[Separatist Droid Army]], by [[22 BBY]],{{TCWcanondates|104}} the first [[Standard year|year]] of the [[Clone Wars]] between the Separatist Alliance and the [[Galactic Republic]].''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' Grievous' habit of using the starfighter to retreat earned it the nickname ''Spineless One'' from his enemies. While the general had a reputation among Republic and Jedi circles for fleeing when the odds were stacked against him, his immediate superiors praised his cautious selections and astute tactical judgements. [[File:General_Grievous_XW2.png|thumb|left|270px|Grievous fleeing the doomed ''Malevolence'']] During the [[Battle of the Kaliida Nebula]], Grievous used the ''Soulless One'' to chase [[Jedi General]]s [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker]] after they boarded the [[Subjugator-class heavy cruiser|''Subjugator''-class heavy cruiser]] ''[[Malevolence]]'' to rescue [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]], whom Grievous had attempted to take hostage in order to prevent the warship's destruction. [[Pilot]]ing the [[G9 Rigger-class light freighter|G9 ''Rigger''-class light freighter]] ''[[Twilight]]'', Skywalker engaged in some tricks, including spinning his [[starship]], in order to evade the ''Soulless One''{{'s}} cannon fire. The ''Malevolence'' was destroyed when it flew into the nearby [[Dead Moon of Antar]] while attempting to jump into [[hyperspace]] due to sabotage by Skywalker. When Grievous was subsequently contacted by Separatist [[Head of State]] [[Count of Serenno|Count]] Dooku regarding an intended rendezvous for the ''Malevolence'', Grievous cut off the transmission and himself escaped into hyperspace. Grievous later used the ''Soulless One'' to escape the [[Battle of Bothawui]], another engagement with Skywalker's forces in [[Bothawui]]'s [[planetary ring]]s. Skywalker attempted to pursue Grievous in [[Anakin Skywalker's Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor|his own starfighter]], but was knocked unconscious due to shrapnel damage from an exploding [[Munificent-class star frigate|''Munificent''-class star frigate]], allowing Grievous to escape.{{TCW|Downfall of a Droid}} Subsequently, Skywalker and a team tracked Grievous to [[Skytop Station]], a secret listening outpost in the atmosphere of the [[moon]] [[Ruusan 2]], and [[Raid on Skytop Station|destroyed]] the facility, leading Grievous to once again depart the scene in the ''Soulless One''.{{TCW|Duel of the Droids}} In [[21 BBY]],{{TCWcanondates|110}} Grievous flew the ''Soulless One'' to his [[Grievous's fortress|personal fortress]] on the moon [[Vassek 3]], landing it inside the [[hangar]] before going to see his [[EV-series medical droid]] [[EV-A4-D]] for maintenance. The General soon discovered that Dooku had [[Mission to Grievous's castle|lured]] [[Jedi Master]] [[Kit Fisto]], [[Jedi Knight]] [[Nahdar Vebb]], and a [[squad]] of [[clone trooper]]s to the fortress as a test of Grievous' skills, leading to a confrontation which only Fisto and his [[astromech droid]] [[R6-H5]] would escape.{{TCW|Lair of Grievous}} ===Grievous' death and afterward=== In [[19 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' when Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker stopped the Separatists from purchasing a giant [[kyber crystal]] on the [[planet]] [[Utapau]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]], Grievous [[Mission to Utapau|intervened]]{{TCW|Crystal Crisis}} and entered the [[Dual Hemisphere-Omni Support Vessel|supply ship]]'s hangar with two [[Vulture-class starfighter|vulture droids]]. However, he fails to prevent the Jedi from blowing up the crystal and fled, chasing them throughout the hangar until an explosion manages to knock his ship out of control in [[Realspace|space]].{{TCW|The Big Bang}} Near the end of the Clone Wars, Grievous brought the ''Soulless One'' to the [[planet]] [[Utapau]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]]. For [[Standard month|months]], the ''Soulless One'' had been docked at a small landing platform above the [[city]]'s [[sinkhole]] on Utapau.{{EncyclopediaCite|Republic and Separatist Ships (2)}} During a lightning attack on the Republic capital world of [[Coruscant]], Grievous was unable to use his personal starfighter, which worked in his advantage because he would have lost it along with his flagship, the ''[[Invisible Hand]]'', if not for that circumstance. In the same years, in the final [[Standard day|days]] of the Clone Wars, Grievous, ever the faithful servant to Darth Sidious,{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|45|History of the Ship}} was ordered to return{{HelmetCollectionCite|24|Highlights of the Saga}} to Utapau, keeping watch over the [[Executive Separatist Council]] while occupying [[Pau City]]. As Grievous had become the Separatist Head of State with Dooku's [[death]] during the [[Battle of Coruscant]], Obi-Wan Kenobi and his [[Cloning|clone]] forces set out for Utapau after learning of Grievous' location from Republic intelligence, beginning the [[Battle of Utapau]]. Kenobi engaged Grievous in a [[lightsaber duel]] which ultimately ended on the ''Soulless One''{{'s}} landing platform, the Jedi resorting to the use of an "uncivilized" [[blaster]] to kill Grievous as he had dropped his [[Obi-Wan Kenobi's third lightsaber|lightsaber]] earlier in the fight. [[File:SunderedHeart-RotS.jpg|thumb|right|265px|Kenobi docked the ''Soulless One'' inside the ''Tantive III'' after using it to escape Utapau.]] As the battle against the remaining [[battle droid]]s continued, [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth]] Sidious, publicly the Republic's [[Supreme Chancellor]] Palpatine, issued [[Order 66]], a command which compelled the [[Grand Army of the Republic]]'s clone [[trooper]]s to turn on and [[Death penalty|execute]] their Jedi [[commanding officer]]s. Kenobi was shot at by the cannon of an [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer]] while he was riding the [[varactyl]] [[Boga]] on the side of the sinkhole, but survived the fall. Sneaking back up through Pau City, the Jedi Master evaded notice and appropriated the ''Soulless One'' to escape Utapau. Once off-planet, Kenobi was contacted by [[Alderaanian]] [[Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]], who had rescued [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]], and a rendezvous was arranged. Upon meeting Organa's [[corvette]], the ''[[Tantive III]]'', Kenobi docked the starfighter with the larger ship's hangar, where it remained docked. During this point, it was briefly owned by Bail Organa. Later, once more, using the late Grievous's starfighter, Kenobi flew to [[Nar Shaddaa]] with a newborn passenger, [[Luke Skywalker]], and sold the ship for [[transport]]ation to the [[desert]] planet [[Tatooine]],{{EncyclopediaCite|Republic and Separatist Ships (2)}} (English version) subsequently bringing Luke there to live with the [[Lars family]]. After that tragic occurrence, the ''Soulless One''{{'s}} ultimate fate was unknown. ==Owners and operators== The ''Soulless One'' was the personal starfighter of General Grievous, the leader of the Separatist Droid Army.{{ForceCollection|General Grievous [Last Stand]|star=5}} After Grievous' death at his hands during the Battle of Utapau, Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi appropriated the starfighter upon surviving Order 66, using it briefly until he went into exile on Tatooine. ==Behind the scenes== The ''Soulless One'' first appeared in the [[2005]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. It was first [[canon]]ically identified as the ''Soulless One'' in the [[2015]] reference book ''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'', and as ''Spineless One'' in the [[2018]] edition of [[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'']]. ==Appearances== *''[[Star Wars: The Prequel Trilogy – A Graphic Novel]]'' *{{TCW|Destroy Malevolence|Destroy ''Malevolence''}} *{{TCW|Downfall of a Droid}} *{{TCW|Duel of the Droids}} *{{TCW|Lair of Grievous}} *{{TCW|Crystal Crisis}} *{{TCW|The Big Bang}} *{{Film|III}} {{1st}} *''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'' ===Non-canon appearances=== *''[[Fortnite]]'' *{{CelebrateTheSeason|All I Want For Life Day}} {{Hologram}} *''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]'' *{{LSWCite|133|A Grievous Getaway}} ==Sources== {{ScrollBox| *{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep104|text="Destroy ''Malevolence''" -
